{"path":"effect_gouraud_shaded_cube_anthropic-claude-sonnet-5_01.html","edit_description":"
Create a complete, self-contained single HTML file implementing a realtime Gouraud-shaded rotating 3D cube using only Canvas 2D (no WebGL, no external libraries). Requirements:

1. Full HTML document with embedded <style> and <script>, dark background, canvas filling most of viewport, centered, with an on-screen HUD showing FPS, wireframe state, and pause state, plus instructions text ("W: toggle wireframe, P: pause/resume").

2. 3D pipeline implemented manually in JS:
   - Define cube as 8 vertices (unit cube, e.g. +-1 on each axis) and 6 faces (each face defined as 4 vertex indices in consistent winding order), plus a base color per face (distinct colors per face, e.g. red, green, blue, yellow, magenta, cyan).
   - Each quad face split into 2 triangles for rasterization.
   - Implement 3D rotation matrices for X, Y, Z axes (functions that take angle and return rotated vertex, or a combined rotation function), applied every frame with time-based angles (rotation accumulates using deltaTime for consistent speed regardless of framerate).
   - Implement a simple perspective projection (project 3D point to 2D screen coords using a focal length / distance from camera, with perspective divide by z).
   - Implement backface culling using the signed area (2D cross product of the projected triangle edges) or using the face normal dot view direction in camera space — compute face/triangle normal in camera space and cull triangles facing away from the camera (normal.z test or dot with view vector).
   - Compute per-vertex normals (for a cube, vertex normal can be same as face normal since faces are flat, but do lighting per-vertex using the face normal, evaluated at each vertex position for the moving light) — implement Lambertian diffuse lighting per vertex: intensity = max(0, dot(normal, lightDir)), plus an ambient term, multiplied against the face base color to get vertex color (RGB).
   - The light source moves over time (e.g. orbits around the cube in a circle/lissajous path), recomputed every frame, and light direction/vector per vertex is recalculated each frame from the current light position and vertex world position.

3. Rasterization:
   - For each visible (non-culled) triangle, rasterize using a scanline / barycentric-coordinate approach on an offscreen ImageData buffer (putImageData) OR using many small filled sub-triangles via canvas fillStyle with gradient approximation. Prefer a real per-pixel barycentric rasterizer operating on a Uint8ClampedArray backing an ImageData for accurate Gouraud (per-pixel interpolated color) shading, with a simple z-buffer (per-pixel depth test) so triangles from different faces composite correctly regardless of draw order.
   - Interpolate vertex colors across each triangle using barycentric coordinates for smooth Gouraud shading (visible color gradients across faces, not flat per-triangle colors).
   - Depth-test per pixel using interpolated 1/z or z, comparing against a z-buffer array sized to canvas resolution (use a reasonably sized internal render resolution, e.g. matching canvas pixel size or a modest downscale like 480x360 upscaled via CSS/canvas width for performance, to keep it real-time smooth).

4. Wireframe toggle (key "W" or "w"): when enabled, draw triangle edges as lines (canvas stroke) on top of or instead of the filled/shaded triangles — should be able to see the wireframe overlay or wireframe-only mode; toggling flips a boolean state.

5. Pause toggle (key "P" or "p"): stops updating rotation angle and light position (freezes animation) but the render loop / FPS counter can keep running or also freeze — a "PAUSED" indicator should show in the HUD when paused.

6. FPS counter: track using requestAnimationFrame timestamps, compute a smoothed/averaged FPS over the last second or via exponential moving average, and display it as an integer in the HUD, updated continuously.

7. Use requestAnimationFrame for the render loop with proper deltaTime calculation (in seconds) so rotation speed is consistent regardless of frame rate; clear/reset z-buffer and pixel buffer each frame before rasterizing.

8. Code should be clean, well-commented, organized into clear sections: math helpers (vector/matrix operations), cube geometry definition, rotation/projection functions, lighting computation, rasterizer (edge function / barycentric per-pixel triangle fill with z-buffer into ImageData), main render loop, and input event listeners for keydown (W/P).

9. No external dependencies, no WebGL, no libraries — pure vanilla JavaScript and Canvas 2D API (getContext('2d'), putImageData/ImageData, or ctx.fillRect per pixel if simpler, but ImageData-based rasterization is preferred for performance and correctness of per-pixel interpolation).

10. Everything must be in this ONE file: HTML structure, CSS styling, and JavaScript logic all inline. Make sure the visual result looks polished (nice dark background, centered canvas with subtle border/shadow, readable HUD text overlay in a corner).

Produce the entire file content now.
"}
